findings.title: Web inline games can freeze on a retried day
findings.description: `run_inline_day` sets `_command_frozen_through = day` under the admission lock, but its two retry exits (`inline_daily_day_budget_exceeded` and `preflight_ok == 0`) return without committing or rolling the frozen day back, and the host is not faulted. In inline mode only the main thread commits days, so a main-thread enqueue in that window loops in `lock_command_admission` waiting on `_control_cv` for `committed_day_value() >= frozen`, a condition that can never become true, and the game hangs for good.

evidence.explanation: The inline day freezes admission before execution. The budget-exceeded and preflight-failure branches push the commands back into `_executor_pending_commands` and return without calling `publish_day`, so `_committed_day` stays at `day-1` and `_command_frozen_through` stays at `day`. `lock_command_admission` skips the wait only on the worker thread. Outside `run_inline_day` the execution context has ended, so a main-thread enqueue whose effective day is no later than the frozen day waits on the cv until the next commit, and that commit can only come from the blocked main thread. Inline mode combined with the native environment happens when `climate_authority_active` and `web_wants_inline` are both true. The adapter comment says the caller retries the same day after pumping peers, so this path is expected rather than exceptional.

findings.title: Runtime guide describes an old handoff
findings.description: The worker no longer waits for main-thread day-tail confirmation between committed days, but `current-state.md` still describes main-thread input preparation and installation of military, vision, and resource results as the daily handoff. A maintainer using that guide to change admission or publication would be working from the removed boundary rather than the current executor-owned path.

## 十二域以外的推进

表外推进者登记在 `tools/ci/runtime_advancers.json` 并生成 `runtime_external_advancers.h`。
理念逐格汇总属于 IDEOLOGY 的日尾阶段。调度由日执行器和主线程交接入口负责。

| 推进者 | 线程 | 读写与交接 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| military | 日执行器与主线程交接 | 主线程冻结 Country/Economy 当日数据并复制 Military 状态。后台计算军务，主线程安装完成的状态并提交 D+1 命令及当日事件。同步模式运行同一计算入口 |
| natural_resource_recovery | 日执行器与主线程交接 | 后台经济更新自己持有的储量。其他资源按原周期冻结到期地块，由同一个执行线程计算，主线程写回地图 |
| bio_occupancy | 日执行器与主线程交接 | 整日模式在资源更新后计算物种存续、引入与扩散。主线程安装整天的结果，再交付科研观察和视野输入。既有存档的物种列恢复到地图与原生数据 |
| season_refresh | 日执行器与主线程交接 | 到期日冻结季节输入，后台计算慢层，主线程在采集次日输入前安装结果。恢复到已结束的某日时仍可提交下一日的季节计算 |
| family / person | 执行线程 | 在经济 FAMILY_COMMIT / PERSON_COMMIT 内运行，没有独立日域 |
| vision | 日执行器与主线程交接 | 领土、玩家军队视野源、探索轨迹或境外观察资格变化时，主线程准备输入，后台计算物理视野、迷雾和科研发现。主线程仍合并探索轨迹、安装结果并提交 D+1 观察记录。开局、读档和同步模式同步解算 |
| ideology_cell_projection | 日执行器与主线程交接 | 主线程从已提交的理念、经济和效果数据冻结目标与指标。后台合成逐格加成，主线程安装结果。旧版效果实例的匹配、发送与回执仍由兼容层处理 |
| visual_delivery | 主线程 | 逐日发出结算通知，其后每帧刷新最新日期。渲染、路线和纹理由实际数据的消费者更新 |
| climate_writeback | 主线程 | 只消费已提交的 Climate 快照写回 slot/MapData |

等上一日结果的输入重试会在同一帧先消费提交，再判断能否发送。天气输入的热赤道采样由后台对冻结的温度和位置计算。日提交直接发布物理场和可复用的风轨迹，主线程把它们写回地图。读档时可用 CLM2 中的物理数据重建首次回写。

年度气候值按环境输入的采样日期读取。第 364 份输入按既有规则采样第 365 日，年末重试时取到同一气候值。

日执行器在当天核心计算提交后完成资源恢复、物种、军务、视野和理念逐格加成汇总。主线程采集输入、安装结果、交付事件、封口命令。
地图纹理上传在同一渲染帧内合并，并在天气插值读取之前提交。

## 前台尚存的模拟工作

以下路径仍需迁移，目标规则见 [design.md](design.md#单一时间线与前后台分工)。

- **输入、交接与次日放行**：主线程仍准备每日输入、安装军务、视野和季节结果，并处理气候、
  资源和物种写回。军务状态复制、视野的探索轨迹合并、D+1 命令和科研观察交接仍在这里。

findings.title: Narrative save silently stores nothing
findings.description: `_write_narrative_provider` writes `bus.capture_story() if bus != null else {}` under the `pknr` key and still returns `ok: true` when the event bus is absent. `DCWorldExt::capture_gameplay_narrative` likewise returns an empty dictionary when no runtime host is present, so a session with a story bus missing saves an empty story section as a success. The matching restore path skips silently for empty input, so the story state is lost on the next load without any error.

citations.citation: Keynes: errors fail loudly instead of falling back silently

evidence.explanation: A missing bus is reported as a successful save with an empty `pknr` section instead of a failure, and the restore side treats the same empty state as nothing to do.

location.code_snippet:
+	var bus = context.get("event_bus")
+	return {"ok": true, "sections": {"pknr": bus.capture_story() if bus != null else {}}}

findings.title: Story saves load without a version check
findings.description: The old GDScript `restore_state` rejected any save whose schema or version did not match with `pknr_schema_incompatible`, and this PR deletes that guard. The replacement `RuntimeNarrative::restore` in runtime_narrative_save.cpp never reads the `version` key the capture writes, fills every missing field with a silent default (for example `_ai_enabled = state.get("ai_enabled", _ai_enabled)`), and installs each field into live members as it decodes. `configure` calls `restore` before any validation, so a save from a different layout is partly installed with defaults instead of being rejected.

evidence.explanation: The removed GDScript block rejected version mismatches explicitly. The surviving C++ restore reads defaults for missing keys, ignores `version`, and writes members directly while decoding, which is the pattern the checklist rejects.

findings.title: Unknown modifiers apply with default id
findings.description: `add_modifier` looks up the effect key's definition in `_modifier_definition_id_by_key_hash` and only assigns `command.definition_id` when the lookup succeeds. When the key is absent, the APPLY packet is still queued with the default definition id, so the modifier is applied under an undefined definition instead of being rejected.

citations.citation: Keynes: errors fail loudly instead of falling back silently

evidence.explanation: The lookup-failure branch sets no error and does not skip the packet. The packet is pushed at line 125 with whatever `definition_id` the struct default holds, so a missing or mistyped modifier key in authored content silently yields an unrecognised modifier.

findings.title: Season history save has no version
findings.description: `RuntimeWorldEnvironment::capture_season_history` writes the view day, the history cursor and both history lanes with no version tag, and `restore_season_history` validates only the byte length and day range. A later change to this layout cannot be told apart from today's bytes, so an older or newer save would be parsed as current and install wrong history without an explicit rejection.

citations.citation: Keynes: new continuation state is versioned, validated and installed atomically

evidence.explanation: The writer emits `day`, `history_next`, then raw lanes with no version field. The reader in `restore_season_history` checks only the total size and cursor range, so no path rejects a format it does not understand.

findings.dismiss_explanation: Project policy: save compatibility is best-effort. Development proceeds as if no old saves exist; no format version bumps, migrations or reject checks are added.

findings.title: Failed narrative payments report success
findings.description: `resolve_narrative_choice()` discards the results of stock-removal and concession-payment submissions, then calls `complete_choice()` even when an economy effect was not accepted. If preflight rejects a command, the economy runtime is unavailable, or the queue is full, the choice and its effect summary are recorded while the stock change or cohort payment is missing, and the finalized choice cannot be submitted again.

citations.citation: Keynes: errors fail loudly instead of falling back silently

evidence.explanation: `submit_economy` returns whether submission succeeded, including false when the economy runtime is null, but `resolve_narrative_choice()` ignores that result for the stock-removal call at line 225 and the concession call at line 241. It then calls `narrative.complete_choice(...)`, which records the choice in the chronicle; a validation or capacity failure can therefore leave an effect unapplied while the choice is recorded as complete.

findings.description: `resolve_narrative_choice()` completes the choice without checking whether submitted economy effects were applied; `submit_economy()` discards the request IDs needed to check their eventual results. findings.title: Rejected army moves can be booked as done
findings.description: `build_pod()` ignores each military economy command's admission outcome and marks every generated row as carried. When queue capacity rejects an embarkation reversal or lane merge, receipt collection does not inspect that rejection and can settle the row using its requested count despite no economy move having occurred.

evidence.explanation: Capacity rejection creates a terminal rejected receipt while `queue_command()` returns true; the new ingress loop ignores all per-command outcomes and leaves rows pending. The military readback path assumes requested counts for disembarkation and merge rather than consuming the rejected receipt.

findings.title: Loaded games lose pending story follow-ups
findings.description: `RuntimeNarrative::capture` saves the last AI-request day and next sequence but omits `_pending_ai` and `_ai_request`, while `restore` also drops a scheduled follow-up’s `ai_requested` marker. If a game is saved while follow-up generation is pending, a cold load publishes no request to resume it, rejects a response with the old sequence, retains the 60-day throttle, and eventually discards the eventless follow-up.

citations.citation: project-keynes-game-flow-runtime

evidence.explanation: Request creation sets the pending state, published request, and last-request day, but capture retains the day and sequence without the pending request, and restore does not reinstate the follow-up’s request marker. Response validation requires the pending sequence, the view publishes the request field, and the retained cooldown prevents a retry before the due day, when the eventless follow-up is removed.

findings.title: Story choices collect no cohort cash

When a player chooses an authored outcome that transfers a percentage of cohort cash to the treasury, `NarrativeEffectAdapter` calculates a zero transfer and treats the effect as simulated.

evidence.explanation: The service passes the native receipt context to the effect adapter, which uses `primary_cohort_cash` to calculate and cap transfers. Authored event outcomes use that percentage-based effect.

findings.title: Annual reports no longer hold the year
findings.description: `AnnualReportSession.before_day()` no longer sets the year-boundary barrier for sessions that are not worker-managed, and `poll()` clears the remaining commit barrier as soon as that day's commit completes. At a year boundary, the clock can advance while the reward is still pending, particularly when another modal delays presentation of the report.

evidence.explanation: The runtime-architecture skill requires checking ownership and timing when a scheduler barrier is removed. The changed session sets only a commit barrier, then clears it based on `last_day` without checking `reward_pending`; report presentation can be deferred by a busy modal.

findings.title: Corrupt terrain save loads silently
findings.description: `NativeMilitaryRuntime::restore_terrain` returns `void` and silently rejects empty or wrong-length saved terrain bytes, while also discarding errors from `set_terrain`. When `attach_military` restores a PKSR military-terrain section that cannot be applied, the load continues with the military core’s current terrain and no diagnostic, allowing the cold-load divergence the section was added to prevent.

citations.citation: Keynes: errors fail loudly instead of falling back silently

evidence.explanation: The save path writes the military-terrain section when the executor owns the environment, but the parser accepts any section length. `attach_military` passes the saved bytes to `restore_terrain`, whose void return and early return on a size mismatch give the caller no failure to handle; it also discards the error string from `set_terrain`. Thus a section can be present but unapplied without the load reporting why.

findings.title: Loaded games lose season history
findings.description: `RuntimeWorldEnvironment::State` starts with no season view, so `refresh_season()` fills the entire history with the current terrain and vegetation on its first refresh. After a cold load, the next season boundary replaces the accumulated history used by the cell display because the newly owned season view is neither saved nor restored.

citations.citation: project-keynes-game-flow-runtime

func _apply_season_display(host, applied: Dictionary) -> void:
	if not applied.has("season_day") or host._current_map == null:
		return
	var map: MapData = host._current_map
	var biome: PackedByteArray = applied.biome_history
	var vegetation: PackedByteArray = applied.vegetation_history
	var next: int = applied.season_history_next
	var cells := map.iter_cells()
	for i in cells.size():
		var cell: HexCell = cells[i]
		if cell == null:
			continue
		if cell.terrain != map.terrain_arr[i]:
			cell.apply_terrain(map.terrain_arr[i])
		cell.landform = map.landform_arr[i]
		cell.vegetation = map.vegetation_arr[i]
		cell.cover = map.cover_arr[i]
		if not cell.current_state.is_empty():
			cell.current_state["biome"] = cell.terrain
			cell.current_state["landform"] = cell.landform
			cell.current_state["vegetation"] = cell.vegetation
			cell.current_state["cover"] = cell.cover
		var begin := i * HexCell.HISTORY_LEN
		cell.biome_history = biome.slice(begin, begin + HexCell.HISTORY_LEN)
		cell.vegetation_history = vegetation.slice(begin, begin + HexCell.HISTORY_LEN)
		cell._history_idx = next

evidence.explanation: The game-flow skill requires complete persistence of native environment authority. The new state owns the rolling history, but the added save payload captures military terrain rather than that view; the first refresh consequently takes the empty-history branch, and the display copies its replacement arrays into cells.

findings.title: Seasonal vegetation changes disappear

findings.title: Generation-gate test can hang instead of failing
findings.description: `runtime_generation_tick_gate_test.gd` replaces the bounded 2400-frame wait for `is_runtime_ready_for_ticks()` with an unbounded `while` loop that only exits on readiness or a recorded generation failure. A world that never becomes ready now stalls the test run rather than failing an expectation. findings.title: Background military events carry no day stamp
findings.description: `NativeSimulationHost::stage_military` calls `military.forward_events(index)` but never sets `military.event_tick = index`, so `forward_events` stamps every record with `record.tick = event_tick`, which is still the initial `-1` or whatever value a save restored. findings.title: Player commands stall the UI for a whole day
findings.description: `lock_command_admission` blocks the calling main thread on `_control_cv` until the in-flight day commits whenever the command's effective day is no later than `_command_frozen_through`. The worker sets that value at the start of each day, so during fast play nearly every UI command, AI reply or narrative choice freezes the frame for the rest of that day's executor work. The PR's comment claims the opposite ("without holding up the executing day"), and the PR description's goal is a main thread that only forwards requests.

evidence.explanation: The worker stores `_command_frozen_through = day` right after draining commands and before executing the day. `_committed_day` only advances in `publish_day` at the end. Main-thread producers (`submit_runtime_command` → `enqueue_batch` → `enqueue_batch_at(seal=true)`) pass a requested day of committed+1, which equals the frozen day, so they wait with no timeout until the commit. Days take several milliseconds (about 4.6 ms on day 114 by the PR's own numbers) and much longer on heavy days.

findings.title: Rejected commands can report a guessed effective date
findings.description: `request_command` now fills `effective_day` in the receipt with the front end's own pre-submit guess (`_next_effective_day()` or the clock day) whenever the simulation result carries neither `effective_day` nor a non-empty `effective_days`. The commit message says receipts must state the date the simulation actually used, but this fallback silently substitutes a UI-computed value for a missing simulation result, so a receipt can show a day the simulation never accepted or assigned. The guess is most likely to surface on rejected or unsupported paths that do not set `effective_day`, and the value is then shown to the player as the command's effective date.

findings.title: AI story follow-ups arrive nine months late
findings.description: `request_ai` always sets the landing day to `input.day + AI_REPLY_DELAY_DAYS` (274), and `followups()` drops the eventless scheduled item once its due day passes. `apply_ai_reply` then re-schedules the generated follow-up at `max(landing_day, due_day)`, so a chain step requested 3 days before it is due shows about 271 days late. 	host._on_clock_day_changed(11)
	host._on_clock_day_changed(12)

	assert(host._climate_capacity_pending_day == -1)

findings.title: Pause check relies on a fixed sleep
findings.description: `_check_annual_report_pause` waits a fixed `OS.delay_msec(100)` and then asserts the committed day stays at `day` and the host state is PAUSED. Elapsed time, not the committed result, decides the check, so a slow executor can look paused and a fast one can finish after the assertion.

citations.citation: Keynes: background-day tests wait for the committed day and receive results

evidence.explanation: The helper advances the environment with `publish_environment_through`, then uses `OS.delay_msec(100)` as its only wait before reading `simulation_committed_day`. Its completion condition is elapsed time rather than a committed-day wait, and the rule asks for `wait_for_runtime_day` plus the host's result-receive step before asserting.

findings.title: Failed regime effects are never retried
findings.description: `settle_player_regime` sets `state.observed_regime = regime` as soon as the REMOVE/APPLY batch is queued, and the next call returns early when `regime == state.observed_regime`, so the `is_permutation` check against the installed Modifier rows never runs again. If the queued batch is rejected when the day commits (for example a stale handle or an entity generation mismatch), the player's political regime Modifier rows stay missing or stale until the regime changes or the session is reloaded. The GDScript `_sync_regime_effects` that this replaces deliberately left its marker empty on failure so that the next commit would retry.

evidence.explanation: The early return at lines 474-475 runs before the installed-row comparison at lines 483-492, and line 520 records the regime as observed when the batch is only enqueued, not when it is applied. The removed GDScript explicitly kept the marker unset on failure so it could retry; the native replacement has no equivalent. `observed_regime` is reset to -1 only on bind (line 381).

findings.title: Corrupt save silently loses queued building changes
findings.description: `EconomyAuthorityTransfer::restore_continuations` decodes the new pending-structure block and, if it is present but fails to decode (`!in.rows(...)` or trailing bytes), clears `pending` and still returns true. The same branch handles an absent block (an empty wire), so a truncated or schema-mismatched block of structural commands is dropped without any error, and the load reports success with structural work missing.

evidence.explanation: The writer emits the block only when `_structural_commands` is non-empty. The reader cannot tell "absent" apart from "present but malformed", and the owned-state validator checks only block framing, not this payload.

findings.title: Economy can apply army moves Military marks failed
findings.description: The rewritten `build_pod` lambda now submits each POD packet one at a time with `submit_economy_pod_command` and returns false on the first rejection, after earlier packets in the same batch were already queued. The caller then sets `receipt_pending = 0` on every authority-2 row, so an Economy population move or lane pay that was actually queued is reported to the military core as failed, and it gets refunded or re-booked while Economy still applies it.

evidence.explanation: The old code submitted the whole set of rows as one `submit_economy_pod_commands(dict)` call and checked a single ok. The new loop is not atomic: packets queued before a failing packet stay queued, yet both failure branches clear the receipt for every authority-2 row, and `run_day` turns those rows into resolved-failed (3).

findings.title: Seasonal vegetation changes never reach army movement
findings.description: `NativeMilitaryRuntime::prepare_day` guards the whole terrain update with `environment.cover != core.terrain().cover`, but the block also copies `vegetation`, `military_base_landform` and `military_settlement_tier`. A seasonal refresh that changes vegetation or landform while cover stays identical is ignored, so military path costs keep using the old vegetation and landform values.

evidence.explanation: Only the cover comparison decides whether `set_terrain` runs. Path cost reads landform and vegetation separately from cover, so changes to those fields alone are lost.

findings.title: One failed background season round halts climate
findings.description: In `SeasonRefreshSystem.tick`, a B+ `fallback` during a background capture sets `background_capture_failed = true`. Only `reset_progress()` clears that flag and `_background_capture_day`, so `run_due_round_for_capture` returns 0 on every later call and `should_run` stays false. Before this change a C++ fallback finished the remaining stages on the micro path; now `_capture_environment` returns `season_refresh_failed` on every later capture, with no retry or fallback.

evidence.explanation: Once the latch is set, both entry points refuse further work until `reset_progress`, and the climate capture keeps returning the failure.
